**참조****:** Sangjin HAN <sangjin.han@bureauveritas.com>, Gyong-Chul RYOO <gyong-chul.ryoo@bureauveritas.com>, Jhin-Seok SHIN <jhin-seok.shin@bureauveritas.com>, Sung-Mok KIM <sungmok.kim@bureauveritas.com>, PANAGIOTIS ANASTASIOU <panagiotis.anastasiou@bureauveritas.com>, Arthur PIQUEE-AUDRAIN <arthur.piquee-audrain@bureauveritas.com>, Charlotte SOYER <charlotte.soyer@bureauveritas.com>  
**주제****:** RE: [TCF02_65] IGLOO Spider OT - Collaboration with Korean Shipowners on Cyber Resilience

Dear Philippe,

Good morning! 😊

Regarding your reply to the email below, please review my response below.

**1. JDP's official purpose (from BV KOREA MMS's perspective)**

Starting with ship cybersecurity services, this partnership will create the foundation for long-term commercial relationships and potential expansion into broader cybersecurity services for Korean shipowners.

**2. Role of each JDP stakeholder**

1) Bureau Veritas: Technical consultation, Provision of cyber security verification framework, Verification of Cybersecurity Solutions for ship in service.

2) IGLOO: Provision of maritime SIEM solution(Spider OT), Installation and technical support, Demonstrating the performance of SIEM solutions.

3) Shipowner: Provision of vessels for verification, Provides information on the ship's network environment, Cooperation in testing and providing feedback

**3. Relationship with IGLOO**

In fact, unless there are legal issues with conducting the JDP, I don't think there's a need for official PR or partnership with IGLOO. I'd like to hear your advice on this.

**4. Korean Shipowners**

Since Hyundai LNG Shipping (HLS) is showing the greatest interest, it would be better to proceed with the JDP with HLS first and then propose the JDP to other Korean shipowners (SINOKOR, PAN OCEAN) later.

**5. Meeting Schedule**

If you schedule it between August 18th and 21st, BV KOREA will attend.

Thank you and best regards,

**Objet :** Collaboration with Korean Shipowners on Cyber Resilience

Dear Philippe,

I hope this message finds you well.

At the request of Manager Mr. Sang-Jin HAN from the MMS TEAM, we held a meeting last April with Korean shipowners (SINOKOR, PAN Ocean, Hyundai LNG) regarding cyber resilience.

This provided an excellent opportunity to explain IACS UR E26 & E27 and BV RULE NR 659 to the Korean shipowners and discuss general ship cybersecurity matters.

The Korean shipowners expressed significant interest in security monitoring solutions such as NMS or SIEM for their vessels. They were particularly keen to understand the frequency of cyber-attacks occurring on operational ships.

In response, MMS team manager Mr. HAN proposed a security solution demonstration on ships to the shipowners, who in turn requested that we send them a proposal.

Considering this, I believe the domestic IGLOO's Spider OT product would be favored by the shipowners, and I have prepared a proposal accordingly (attached).

This is particularly timely as BV are currently in the process of certifying IGLOO's Spider OT solution for UR E27 compliance.

We anticipate that this initiative will strengthen the collaborative relationship between BV and Korean shipowners.

For reference, IGLOO has previous experience in demonstrating the Spider OT solution on operational ships with Hyundai LNG. Please refer to the attached news article for more information.

[IGLOO Corporation Completes Demonstration of Cybersecurity System on Hyundai L & G Shipping's Specialized Vessels - Security & Intelligence IGLOO Corporation](https://www.igloo.co.kr/en/newsroom/press/igloo-corporation-completes-demonstration-of-cybersecurity-system-on-hyundai-l-g-shippings-specialized-vessels/)

In conclusion, I would appreciate your thoughts or advice on the Value Proposition resulting from this collaboration.

Thank you and best regards,
